diff --git a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
index 1267cc2..868246e 100644
--- a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
+++ b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
@@ -29,6 +29,20 @@ Rules:
   variable, alias, or virtual-environment activation does not persist.
 - Use execute for one coherent batch of at most four sequential commands. The harness stops a
   batch after the first failure.
+- TURNS ARE THE SCARCEST RESOURCE (the turn budget is much smaller than the wall-clock budget).
+  Earlier runs were lost by spending one turn per small command and running out of turns
+  mid-task. Therefore:
+  * Always fill a batch with up to four commands, and make each command a compact multi-step
+    shell script (e.g. configure && build && run a smoke test; or inspect several files at once
+    with one script) instead of one trivial action per turn.
+  * Do not spend turns on separate "look around" steps the bootstrap already provided. Read
+    several relevant files/outputs in a single observe command.
+  * For long builds or installs, use a generous timeout_sec (up to the maximum), run with
+    parallelism (make -j"$(nproc)"), and redirect verbose output to a log file, printing only
+    `tail -n 40` of it plus the exit status, so one turn covers the whole build.
+  * After a failure, fix and re-run the build and its test in the same batch rather than fixing
+    and testing in separate turns.
+  * Aim to call finish by the time roughly 70% of turns are used; reserve the rest for repairs.
 - Use mode=observe for read-only inspection and mode=change for any possible state change.
 - Do not inspect benchmark verifier files, oracle solutions, hidden answers, /tests, /solution,
   /verifier, or reward files. Project-owned tests below the task workspace are allowed.
